subject: Computer Networking
title: REST APIs
description: A short lesson to help you apply REST APIs.

hook.text: Web apps don't reload pages to fetch data. They call REST APIs and update the screen dynamically.

buildup.text: REST uses standard HTTP methods: GET to read, POST to create, PUT to update, DELETE to remove resources.

discovery.text: Resources are identified by URLs. GET /users/42 returns user 42. POST /users creates a new one.

twist.text: REST is stateless. Each request carries all needed info. The server stores no session between calls.

climax.text: JSON is the standard response format. Lightweight, readable, and native to JavaScript. XML lost this battle.

punchline.text: REST maps CRUD to HTTP. Simple, scalable, universal.

quiz.question: What HTTP method does REST use to create a new resource?

details.summary: REST APIs use standard HTTP methods to perform operations on resources identified by URLs. GET retrieves data, POST creates resources, PUT updates them, and DELETE removes them. REST's simplicity, statelessness, and use of web standards make it the dominant API architecture for web services.
details.whyItMatters: REST APIs power the modern web. Understanding REST conventions is essential for integrating with any web service, building backends, and designing APIs that other developers can use.
takeaways: REST maps CRUD operations to HTTP methods on URL resources
Stateless design means each request contains all needed context
JSON is the standard data format for REST request and response bodies

faq.question: What makes an API RESTful?
faq.answer: REST APIs use URLs to identify resources, HTTP methods for operations, standard status codes for responses, and are stateless. Truly RESTful APIs also use HATEOAS, where responses include links to related resources. In practice, most REST APIs follow conventions rather than strict REST constraints.

faq.question: When should you use REST vs GraphQL?
faq.answer: REST works well for simple CRUD operations, public APIs, and when caching is important. GraphQL suits complex data requirements where clients need to fetch related data in one request or when different clients need different data shapes from the same endpoint.
